entities.summary: Urbain de Maillé, 1st Marquis of Brézé, was a 17th-century French soldier and diplomat who played a pivotal role in shaping the course of European history. Born in Brézé, France in 1597, he rose to prominence as a Marshal of France and Ambassador to Sweden in 1632. His tenure as Viceroy of Catalonia from 1641 to 1642 had a lasting impact on the region. De Maillé's legacy can be seen in the establishment of the French monarchy's centralized power structure and the development of the country's diplomatic corps. He was instrumental in the Peace of Westphalia, a treaty that ended the Thirty Years' War and cemented the borders of modern-day Germany. De Maillé's contributions to the French military and diplomatic endeavors have made him a significant figure in the annals of European history. His diplomatic success in Sweden and his leadership in Catalonia left a lasting impression on the region, solidifying his place as one of the most influential figures of the 17th century. Despite his passing in 1650, de Maillé's impact on European politics and diplomacy continues to be felt today.
